rapport_notes: Warm and reassuring, especially in directly addressing the customer's stated fear about item damage from a past bad move; built trust before quoting.

evidence_quotes.agenda: 'before we go any further, did you have any just concerns or questions so far?' — asked only after date, name, email, address, square footage, garage, and packing had already been covered.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said prior movers damaged her things and 'that is absolutely important to me that they're wrapping done.' Rep answered with one solid reassurance (in-house movers, $2,000 coverage) but did not ask a follow-up like 'anything else that worries you about it?' — one question, one answer.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'we don't work with daily contractors... [movers] work for the actual [company]' (commit-to-rate/experience) and 'if it ends up being three hours... that's all you'll pay for anyway' (beats-it-pay-less).

top_strength: Directly and warmly addressed the customer's stated fear about item damage from a past bad move, using the no-worries damage coverage and in-house (non-contractor) mover framing to build real trust before ever quoting a price.
coaching_note: The agenda question came only after logistics had already started, costing the full 10 points — asking it as the very first thing (before date/name/address) would have surfaced the damage concern immediately and let it shape the whole call. On-Time Guarantee and Meet Your Mover were also never mentioned.
